Attention is firmly on the Bank of Japan now, which meets tomorrow and is widely expected to leave its policy rate unchanged, with money markets assigning only a small probability to a surprise move. The real focus will be the accompanying quarterly outlook report and Governor Ueda's press conference for any signal on whether the next hike lands in the autumn or later in the year. With the yen trading close to levels that have previously triggered intervention from Japanese authorities, any dovish surprise carries the risk of a sharp reaction.
currencies.watchToday: Japan's unemployment rate and then retail sales and industrial production data are due later today, but they are typically minor movers. The main event is tomorrow, with Tokyo core inflation, the Bank of Japan's rate decision and Governor Ueda's press conference all landing in quick succession.

currencies.headline: Franc ticks firmer as Middle East tensions and softer equities lend mild safe-haven support.
currencies.commentary:
The Swiss franc has picked up a modest safe-haven bid this afternoon as renewed fighting in the Middle East and a shakier tone across global equity markets have encouraged some investors back into traditionally defensive currencies. There has been no domestic Swiss data to drive the move; instead the franc is largely trading off the same forces moving the yen and gold, with geopolitical risk and uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's next steps doing most of the work.

With Swiss inflation already running well below most other major economies, the franc's safe-haven role remains its primary driver for now rather than any prospect of near-term policy change from the Swiss National Bank. That dynamic is likely to persist into tomorrow, when the KOF Economic Barometer offers the next real read on the domestic economy, though it is rarely a big mover for the currency compared with shifts in broader risk appetite.
currencies.watchToday: There is no further Swiss-specific data due today. Tomorrow's KOF Economic Barometer at 07:00 is the next domestic release, with Swiss inflation data not due until Monday.

currencies.headline: Loonie gets a lift from rising oil prices, though trade frictions continue to cap the gains.
currencies.commentary:
The Canadian dollar has found some support this afternoon as crude oil extends its climb for a third straight session, with renewed fighting in the Middle East reviving concerns about supply disruption. As an oil-linked currency, the loonie would normally be expected to track such a move fairly closely, and it has firmed modestly as a result, though the advance has been more muted than the scale of the oil move might suggest.

The gap between the two reflects an ongoing drag from trade friction with the United States, which has weighed on the currency for weeks and has made it a laggard even during periods when oil has rallied hard. Until that overhang clears, gains from higher energy prices are likely to keep being only partially reflected in the exchange rate. There is no Canadian data due for the rest of today.
currencies.watchToday: No further Canadian data are scheduled for today. The next release is tomorrow's GDP by industry report for May, with a June advance estimate, at 13:30, which will offer an early read on how the economy is tracking into the third quarter.

currencies.headline: Kiwi dollar little changed, holding onto this morning's business confidence boost.
currencies.commentary:
The New Zealand dollar has been quiet this afternoon, with little fresh domestic news to add to this morning's sharply improved ANZ business confidence survey. That reading showed a broad based lift in sentiment, with exporters, investment and employment intentions all firmer, and the currency has held onto most of the modest support that provided earlier in the session.

With no further New Zealand data due and broader risk appetite mixed following the Federal Reserve's non-committal tone and renewed Middle East tensions, the kiwi has largely tracked moves in its more heavily traded peers this afternoon rather than setting its own direction. Trade-linked currencies including the New Zealand dollar are likely to take more direction from tomorrow's Chinese manufacturing data than from anything domestic in the short term.
currencies.watchToday: No further New Zealand data are due today. China's NBS manufacturing PMI tomorrow morning is worth watching given the close trade relationship, alongside the private Caixin equivalent early next week.

currencies.headline: Aussie dollar softer as risk appetite wobbles and traders look to tomorrow's Chinese data.
currencies.commentary:
The Australian dollar has drifted lower this afternoon alongside a broader softening in risk appetite, as renewed fighting in the Middle East and an unusually vague Federal Reserve press conference have left investors a little more cautious than they were earlier in the week. As a currency that tends to track global growth and risk sentiment closely, the Aussie dollar has been among the more sensitive movers to that shift, alongside a similarly soft session for equities.

There has been no fresh Australian-specific news today to offset that backdrop. The currency remains not far from levels seen after Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock's balanced remarks earlier this week, in which she left the door open to further tightening without giving markets a clear signal on timing. That leaves the currency leaning on external drivers, in particular China's economic data given the trade relationship between the two economies.
currencies.watchToday: No Australian data are due for the rest of today. China's NBS manufacturing PMI tomorrow morning is the next notable release with a direct bearing on the Aussie dollar, given how closely the two economies are linked through trade.

currencies.headline: Yuan steady as markets look ahead to tomorrow's manufacturing PMI.
currencies.commentary:
The Chinese yuan has been broadly stable this afternoon, with little domestic news to move it and onshore markets taking their cue instead from the softer global risk tone following this week's Federal Reserve meeting and renewed Middle East tensions. There has been no fresh Chinese data released today.

The People's Bank of China has continued to add to its gold reserves in recent months, a sign of the broader diversification push that has been a feature of Chinese reserve management this year, though this is a slow moving trend rather than a same-day driver of the currency. The more immediate focus is tomorrow's official manufacturing PMI, which will offer the first proper read on how Chinese factories performed in July and is likely to matter as much for the Australian and New Zealand dollars as for the yuan itself given the trade links involved.
currencies.watchToday: China's NBS manufacturing PMI for July is due first thing tomorrow morning and is the next significant release, with the private Caixin manufacturing survey following early next week.

currencies.headline: Rand steady, with little fresh domestic news to move it this afternoon.
currencies.commentary:
The South African rand has traded quietly this afternoon, with no domestic data or headlines of note to shift the currency out of its recent range. Broader risk sentiment has softened slightly following an unusually non-committal Federal Reserve press conference this week and renewed fighting in the Middle East, a combination that has typically weighed a little on emerging market currencies including the rand, though the moves have been modest so far.

Gold's role as a safe-haven asset has offered the rand some offsetting support given South Africa's position as a major producer, even as broader risk appetite has cooled. With no local data due for the rest of today, the currency is likely to keep taking its cue from global rather than domestic drivers into the end of the week.
currencies.watchToday: No South African data are due for the rest of today. The next notable domestic event is SARB Governor Lesetja Kganyago's address to the Reserve Bank's annual general meeting tomorrow morning, watched for any signals ahead of September's Monetary Policy Committee meeting.

currencies.headline: Sterling softens as a firmer dollar dominates ahead of back to back central bank decisions.
currencies.commentary:
Sterling has drifted lower overnight, giving back some of yesterday's gains as the dollar firms broadly ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision. There's no fresh UK-specific news behind the move, it's largely a function of traders turning cautious and adding to dollar positions ahead of what's shaping up to be an unusually dense week of central bank action.

This week is genuinely unusual: the Fed, Bank of England and Bank of Japan all meet within three days of each other, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday respectively. That clustering tends to keep individual currencies more reactive to the broad dollar mood than to their own fundamentals until each decision actually lands, which is largely what's playing out for sterling this morning.
currencies.watchToday: Nothing further is scheduled for GBP today. Attention builds toward Thursday's Bank of England decision (Bank Rate currently 3.75%), where a new Monetary Policy Report will be published alongside the vote.

currencies.headline: Euro consolidates near its recent lows as traders await the Fed.
currencies.commentary:
The euro has been stuck in a narrow range overnight, hovering close to its weakest levels of the past month as the broader dollar firms across the board. Traders appear reluctant to place aggressive bets in either direction with the two-day FOMC meeting concluding tomorrow, preferring to wait for the outcome before committing.

With the ECB on hold and no fresh Eurozone data overnight, the euro's next real catalyst is domestic rather than external: Thursday brings both German and Eurozone flash GDP for the second quarter, followed by Friday's Eurozone flash inflation print, either of which could move the currency more than today's quiet session.
currencies.watchToday: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel speaks this morning (09:00 UK time), watched closely for any shift in tone on the path of rates. Governing Council member Pierre Wunsch follows this afternoon (13:00), though his remarks are typically lower profile.

currencies.headline: Dollar holds at a one month high as traders keep a hike back on the table.
currencies.commentary:
The dollar has firmed further overnight to its strongest level in around a month, as markets continue to price a slim but real chance that the Fed surprises with a rate hike at tomorrow's decision rather than the widely expected hold. That two-sided uncertainty, hold versus hike, is unusual this late in a cycle and is part of why the dollar has been able to grind higher even after yesterday's sharp pullback on easing Middle East tensions.

The press conference that follows tomorrow's decision will likely matter more than the decision itself for how the dollar trades afterwards, since that's typically where the Fed Chair gives the clearest signal on the pace and timing of any further moves. Markets are essentially using today's session to position ahead of that.
currencies.watchToday: US Conference Board Consumer Confidence data lands this afternoon (15:00 UK time), followed by a speech from Fed Governor Christopher Waller at 17:00, both of which could shift expectations further ahead of tomorrow's rate decision.

currencies.headline: Yen holds flat near four decade lows as the dollar's firmness dominates.
currencies.commentary:
The yen has been broadly flat against the dollar overnight, continuing to linger near its weakest level in roughly four decades as the dollar's own firmness, rather than any fresh yen-specific news, keeps the pair pinned near recent extremes. With the Fed decision tomorrow and the Bank of Japan's own meeting concluding Friday, traders appear content to wait rather than push the pair meaningfully in either direction today.

That calm is unlikely to last: this week features Japan's national CPI print on Thursday and Friday's BoJ decision, where the central bank is expected to hold but faces growing pressure to signal a faster path of future hikes. Any hawkish shift in tone from Governor Ueda would likely matter far more for the yen than today's quiet overnight session.
currencies.watchToday: Nothing further is scheduled for JPY today. Japan's national CPI print lands Thursday, setting the stage for Friday's Bank of Japan decision (rate currently 1.00%).

currencies.headline: Franc weakens toward its softest level in over a year as fresh US tariffs bite.
currencies.commentary:
The franc has slipped against the dollar overnight, trading close to its weakest level in more than a year, as the broader dollar firms and fresh details emerge on US tariffs affecting Swiss imports. Washington has confirmed those tariffs will stay within the ceiling previously announced, which removes some uncertainty but keeps a genuine headwind in place for a Swiss economy that relies heavily on exports.

That combination, a firmer dollar and a confirmed tariff burden, is a more specifically CHF-negative story than the broad market mood alone would suggest. With no Swiss data due domestically this week beyond Friday's KOF Barometer, the franc is likely to keep tracking both the dollar's direction and any further tariff-related headlines rather than its own fundamentals.
currencies.watchToday: No CHF-specific events are scheduled today. The KOF Economic Barometer is due Friday, alongside broader dollar direction into Wednesday's Fed decision, as the main things to watch this week.

currencies.headline: Loonie near a two week low as oil's slide deepens and the BoC stays dovish.
currencies.commentary:
The Canadian dollar has weakened to its softest level in roughly two weeks this morning, weighed down by a further slide in oil prices and a Bank of Canada seen as leaning dovish after last month's hold. Oil has now dropped sharply from last week's highs as the pause in US-Iran hostilities continues to hold, and with Canada a major energy exporter, that decline is doing more damage to the loonie than the broader dollar mood is helping other currencies.

That said, the same de-escalation capping oil prices is also capping how far the dollar itself can run, which is providing some offsetting support. Speculative positioning against the loonie has reportedly been trimmed in recent sessions, suggesting some traders see the current weakness as closer to a floor than a fresh trend.
currencies.watchToday: The Bank of Canada's Summary of Deliberations from its most recent decision is due this evening (18:30 UK time), which could offer clues on how divided policymakers were and what might come next.

currencies.headline: Kiwi softens as the firmer dollar and a broader bond selloff weigh.
currencies.commentary:
The New Zealand dollar has eased overnight alongside the Australian dollar, as a broadly firmer US dollar and a selloff in government bond markets both weigh on higher-yielding currencies. It's a reversal from yesterday afternoon's relief rally, when easing Middle East tensions had briefly lifted risk appetite and the kiwi along with it.

The underlying story for NZD hasn't fundamentally changed: this month's RBNZ hike and hawkish signals for further tightening still provide a floor of support, but with the next Official Cash Rate decision not until September, the kiwi is likely to keep taking its cues mainly from the broader dollar and global risk mood rather than domestic developments in the near term.
currencies.watchToday: No New Zealand data is due today. With the next RBNZ meeting not until September, the kiwi is likely to stay reactive to broader dollar moves and Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Aussie eases as government bonds sell off and the dollar firms.
currencies.commentary:
The Australian dollar has softened this morning as a broader selloff in government bonds and a firmer US dollar both weigh on sentiment, giving back some of yesterday's gains from the pullback in oil prices. Australia's own inflation data lands tomorrow and is likely to matter more for direction than today's broader market mood.

That inflation print carries real weight for the Reserve Bank of Australia's thinking heading into its mid-August meeting, where markets are still debating the odds of a further hike. China's economic performance remains the other key swing factor given how much of Australia's exports go there, and a Chinese manufacturing survey due later this week will add to that picture.
currencies.watchToday: Australia's second quarter CPI print lands overnight tonight into tomorrow (02:30 UK time), the most important domestic data point ahead of the RBA's mid-August meeting.

currencies.headline: Yuan steady as traders await China's manufacturing snapshot later this week.
currencies.commentary:
The offshore yuan has been little changed overnight, continuing the relative stability that's characterised its trading in recent weeks even as the broader dollar has firmed against most other majors. The PBoC continues to manage the currency mainly through its daily fixing rather than large moves, which is part of why CNY tends to see smaller swings than higher-beta currencies during periods of dollar strength.

The more interesting test comes later this week with China's official manufacturing survey, a timely read on how the world's second largest economy is tracking and a release that matters not just for the yuan but for AUD and NZD too, given how closely both are tied to Chinese demand.
currencies.watchToday: China's official NBS Manufacturing PMI for July is due Friday, the main domestic release to watch this week alongside broader dollar direction into Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Rand extends its slide to a fresh two month low after last week's surprise SARB hold.
currencies.commentary:
The rand has weakened further overnight to its softest level since mid-May, continuing to digest last week's SARB decision to hold its policy rate steady when markets had widely expected a hike. That dovish surprise, combined with South African inflation running at a two-year high, has left the currency exposed at a moment when the broader dollar is also firming across the board.

The combination is a difficult one for the rand: a central bank seen as reluctant to raise rates further even as inflation runs hot, at the same time as global dollar strength adds an external headwind. With no SARB meeting scheduled this week, the rand is likely to stay sensitive to broader dollar moves and any further Middle East developments rather than domestic news.
currencies.watchToday: No SARB meeting is scheduled this week. The rand is likely to stay driven by external factors, particularly broader dollar direction into Wednesday's Fed decision, rather than domestic news.

currencies.headline: Sterling firm as traders price in higher odds of a BoE hike, not a cut.
currencies.commentary:
GBP has held up well over the past week as a rebound in oil prices, driven by renewed Middle East tensions, has pushed UK inflation expectations higher. Higher energy costs feed fairly directly into the UK's inflation basket, so when oil rallies, markets tend to reassess how much room the Bank of England actually has to cut rates further this year.

That reassessment has been fairly dramatic: a recent Reuters poll of economists found nearly 40% now expect at least one further Bank of England hike this year, a marked shift from earlier expectations of a rate cut. Markets are now pricing in the possibility of two hikes by March 2027. For context, sterling has generally taken its direction over the past year from the gap between UK and US/Eurozone interest rate expectations, so a more hawkish repricing of the Bank of England tends to support the pound relative to currencies where central banks are seen as more likely to ease.
currencies.watchToday: No major UK data due today, so sterling is likely to stay largely reactive to broader dollar and euro moves rather than its own news. Attention is building toward Thursday's Bank of England decision (Bank Rate currently 3.75%), where a new Monetary Policy Report will be published alongside the vote; that report's growth and inflation forecasts will matter as much as the rate decision itself for where sterling goes next.

currencies.headline: Euro steady after the ECB held rates last week.
currencies.commentary:
The ECB left its deposit rate unchanged at 2.25% at its 23 July meeting, keeping policy on hold amid ongoing energy-driven uncertainty. Christine Lagarde's post-meeting comments were read as fairly balanced, giving the market little fresh reason to move euro rate expectations in either direction.

With no ECB meeting scheduled this week, EUR direction is more likely to be driven by upcoming Eurozone growth and inflation data than by fresh central bank action. Germany's economy, as the bloc's largest, tends to have an outsized influence on how the euro reacts to Eurozone-wide releases, so growth or inflation surprises out of Germany specifically are usually worth watching a little more closely than the headline Eurozone figure alone.
currencies.watchToday: A quiet start to the week for the euro, with no major data releases scheduled today. ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel, whose remarks are watched closely for any shift in tone on the path of rates, speaks tomorrow, followed by flash Q2 GDP and inflation data from Germany and the wider Eurozone later in the week, both of which have the potential to move EUR more than this week's speeches.

currencies.headline: Dollar in a holding pattern ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.
currencies.commentary:
The Federal Reserve is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at 3.50%-3.75% this week, though markets are assigning a meaningful probability to a surprise hike given recent inflation pressure. That two-sided uncertainty is part of why the dollar has traded in a relatively tight range over the past few sessions. With a genuine chance of either outcome, investors have less conviction to push the currency firmly in one direction ahead of the announcement.

The press conference that follows Wednesday's decision will likely matter more than the rate decision itself for how USD trades afterwards, since that's typically where the Fed Chair gives the clearest signal on the likely pace and timing of any further moves this year.
currencies.watchToday: No major US releases today, leaving the dollar to take its cues mainly from positioning ahead of Wednesday. Consumer confidence data and a speech from Fed Governor Christopher Waller are due tomorrow, both of which could shift expectations one way or the other heading into the rate decision itself.

currencies.headline: Yen extends its slide to a fresh 40-year low ahead of Friday's BoJ decision.
currencies.commentary:
The yen has continued weakening against the dollar, touching a fresh four-decade low even as Japanese officials repeat warnings that they are ready to intervene if moves become disorderly. That warning has done little to slow the drop so far, a sign that broad dollar strength and a wide gap between US and Japanese interest rates are currently outweighing intervention risk in traders' minds.

Attention is turning to Friday's Bank of Japan meeting, where the BoJ is expected to hold rates steady but is under growing pressure to signal a faster path of future hikes. Inflation pressure has been building from the weaker yen itself, robust global demand tied to AI-related spending, and higher energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict. A central bank holding rates but leaning hawkish in tone tends to matter more for direction than the decision itself, since it's the shift in expectations for future moves, not this week's outcome, that typically drives USD/JPY.
currencies.watchToday: Japan's national CPI print on Thursday will set the stage for Friday's Bank of Japan decision (rate currently 1.00%), where the central bank is expected to hold but may lean hawkish given the inflation pressure described above. Governor Ueda's post-meeting press conference will likely matter more for the yen than the decision itself.

currencies.headline: Franc holds unusually strong as the SNB keeps the door open to negative rates.
currencies.commentary:
The Swiss National Bank left its policy rate unchanged at 0% at its June meeting, as widely expected, while making clear that a return to negative rates has not been ruled out if the franc's strength and soft inflation persist. EUR/CHF has stayed unusually strong for an extended period this year, reflecting the franc's traditional role as a safe haven at a time when Middle East tensions and elevated oil prices have kept broader risk sentiment fragile.

That safe haven demand is the key mechanism behind the franc's recent resilience: when geopolitical risk rises, investors tend to buy CHF regardless of what Swiss interest rates are doing, which is part of why the SNB has signalled greater readiness to intervene directly in the currency market rather than relying on rates alone. For clients, that means the franc can behave differently from other majors during periods of stress, often strengthening even as more growth-sensitive currencies come under pressure.
currencies.watchToday: No Swiss-specific data releases are being tracked this week; CHF trading is more likely to be driven by broader safe-haven flows tied to Middle East developments and this week's Fed decision than by anything scheduled domestically.

currencies.headline: Loonie steadies as rising oil offsets US tariff uncertainty.
currencies.commentary:
The Canadian dollar has firmed from last week's pullback, supported by a rally in oil prices as fighting around the Strait of Hormuz and threats from Yemen's Ansar Allah raise fresh concerns about Middle Eastern crude supply. The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% at its mid-July meeting while raising its 2026 inflation projection, and expects inflation to return to its 2% target by early 2027.

Oil remains one of the more reliable drivers of CAD given Canada's status as a major energy exporter, so the recent rally has provided some support even as fresh US tariffs on Canadian goods create a separate headwind. With those two forces pulling in opposite directions, USD/CAD has stayed range bound for weeks, and most bank forecasts see that easing only gradually over the coming months rather than moving sharply either way.
currencies.watchToday: No major Canadian releases are due today. With the Bank of Canada's next decision some weeks away, the loonie is likely to keep taking its cues mainly from oil prices and the broader dollar backdrop around Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Kiwi extends its rebound after the RBNZ's first hike in three years.
currencies.commentary:
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand raised the Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on 8 July, its first hike since May 2023, and a stronger than expected inflation report released on 20 July has reinforced expectations of further tightening. Annual consumer price inflation accelerated to 4.1%, driven largely by a surge in fuel prices tied to the Middle East conflict, with petrol up more than 27% year on year.

Analysts now expect the RBNZ to hike again at both its September and October meetings, taking the OCR toward 3% by year end, which has helped the kiwi hold most of its recent gains. New Zealand's reliance on imported oil is a genuine vulnerability though: further escalation in the Middle East would push fuel costs, and inflation, higher still, but could also dent risk appetite in a way that weighs on a currency that tends to trade like a barometer for broader global sentiment.
currencies.watchToday: No New Zealand data is due today. With the next RBNZ meeting not until September, the kiwi is likely to stay reactive to broader dollar moves and Wednesday's Fed decision rather than its own news this week.

currencies.headline: Aussie firms as traders lift bets on an RBA hike.
currencies.commentary:
AUD/USD has firmed, supported by growing expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise rates again, with markets now pricing roughly a one in four chance of a move at the RBA's August meeting and better than even odds by December. Firmer domestic activity data has added to that repricing over the past week.

China's economic performance remains the other major swing factor for the Australian dollar, since China buys around a third of Australia's exports and is the key source of demand for iron ore, coal and gas. China's economy grew 4.3% year on year in the second quarter, its weakest pace in three years, a reminder that a soft Chinese growth backdrop can offset even a hawkish RBA. For now, AUD/USD looks likely to stay within a broad range for now.
currencies.watchToday: No major Australian data is due today, though this week's Fed decision and any fresh signal on China or commodity demand are likely to matter more for AUD than domestic news, ahead of Australian inflation and labour data due before the 11 August RBA meeting.

currencies.headline: Yuan holds steady as Beijing deepens Hong Kong's role as an offshore hub.
currencies.commentary:
The offshore yuan has been broadly stable this month after the People's Bank of China announced a set of structural measures aimed at cementing Hong Kong's position as the main offshore centre for yuan trading, including higher caps on cross border bond and currency facilities. Governor Pan Gongsheng said international demand for the yuan is broadening beyond simple trade settlement into investment and reserve holdings, though the PBoC gave no fresh signal on near term rate cuts.

The PBoC's approach continues to prioritise stability over sharp moves in either direction, managing the currency mainly through its daily fixing rather than large rate changes, which is why CNY tends to be one of the least volatile major currencies clients trade day to day. Several banks expect gradual yuan strength over the rest of 2026, but any shift usually plays out over weeks and months rather than in a single session.
currencies.watchToday: No CNY-specific events are being tracked this week; the yuan's daily fixing and any fresh PBoC commentary on Hong Kong's offshore role remain the main things to watch, alongside broader dollar direction around Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Rand weakens as a hawkish Fed and rising oil weigh on the currency.
currencies.commentary:
USD/ZAR has pushed higher to a two month low for the rand, as a more hawkish Federal Reserve stance and rising oil prices linked to Middle East tensions both work against emerging market currencies like the rand. The South African Reserve Bank left its repo rate unchanged at 7.00% at its July meeting, a decision passed on a split 4 to 2 vote, despite markets having expected at least a quarter point hike.

South African inflation accelerated to 5.0% in June, which puts the SARB in a difficult position: raising rates further would support the currency but risks weighing on an already fragile growth outlook, while holding steady, as it just did, leaves the rand more exposed to swings in broader risk appetite and the dollar. As an oil importer, South Africa is also directly exposed to the recent rise in crude prices, which adds further inflation pressure at an awkward moment.
currencies.watchToday: No SARB meeting is scheduled this week, so the rand is likely to stay driven by external factors, particularly Wednesday's Fed decision and any further moves in oil prices tied to the Middle East, rather than domestic news.

currencies.headline: Sterling drifts higher as a broadly softer dollar outweighs a quiet UK session.
currencies.commentary:
Sterling has ticked higher this afternoon, largely on the back of broad dollar weakness rather than any fresh UK-specific news. The main story of the session has been a sharp reversal in oil prices, down roughly 9%, after the US and Iran paused their military strikes over the weekend, which has pulled the dollar broadly lower and eased the safe haven bid that had been building since the fighting began.

With nothing scheduled domestically today, sterling's afternoon move has essentially been a mirror image of the dollar's retreat rather than a story of its own. That said, this morning's hawkish repricing around Thursday's Bank of England decision still stands, and it's that gap between UK and US/Eurozone rate expectations, not today's session, that remains the bigger driver of where sterling goes from here.
currencies.watchToday: Nothing further is scheduled for GBP today. Attention now turns to the week's other central bank events, with the focus firmly on Wednesday's Fed decision and Thursday's Bank of England meeting (Bank Rate currently 3.75%).

currencies.headline: Euro edges up but stays capped as oil's slide eases inflation worries.
currencies.commentary:
The euro has firmed modestly this afternoon, helped by the same broad dollar retreat lifting most majors today, but remains boxed into the tight range it has held since Friday. Brent crude's roughly 9% drop, after the US and Iran paused hostilities over the weekend, has taken some pressure off the energy-driven inflation concerns that have weighed on the single currency in recent weeks.

Even so, the market still expects a fairly hawkish tone from the Fed at Wednesday's meeting, which is limiting how far the euro can run on dollar weakness alone. With the ECB on hold and no fresh Eurozone data today, the euro's next real test comes from Thursday's German and Eurozone GDP releases rather than anything in today's session.
currencies.watchToday: No EUR events remain scheduled for today. ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel speaks tomorrow morning (09:00 UK time), followed later in the week by flash Q2 GDP and inflation data from Germany and the wider Eurozone, both more likely to move the euro than today's quiet session.

currencies.headline: Dollar pulls back broadly as the US and Iran pause hostilities for a third night.
currencies.commentary:
The dollar has slipped modestly this afternoon, its softest level in around a week, after the US and Iran paused their strikes over the weekend for a third consecutive night to make room for diplomacy. That de-escalation has sharply reduced the safe haven premium that had been building in the dollar since fighting began, and Brent crude's roughly 9% slide today has reinforced the move.

The bigger event for the dollar this week is still ahead: Wednesday's Fed decision, where futures markets are assigning a meaningful, if still minority, probability to a surprise hike given recent inflation pressure. Today's pullback is best read as a reset of the geopolitical risk premium rather than a shift in Fed expectations, which remain the dominant force likely to drive the dollar for the rest of the week.
currencies.watchToday: No US data is scheduled for the remainder of today. Consumer confidence figures and a speech from Fed Governor Christopher Waller are due tomorrow, both of which could shift expectations further ahead of Wednesday's rate decision.

currencies.headline: Yen firms modestly as the dollar's safe haven bid fades.
currencies.commentary:
USD/JPY has eased slightly this afternoon, down a touch from this morning, as the broad dollar retreat following the US-Iran strike pause has taken some of the wind out of the pair's recent run toward 40-year highs. Traders largely shrugged off renewed warnings from Japan's Finance Ministry that it stands ready to intervene if moves become disorderly, treating today's move as dollar-driven rather than yen-driven.

Reports that some Bank of Japan officials are open to raising rates faster than markets currently expect have added a little independent support for the yen today, though the bigger tests remain ahead: Thursday's national CPI print and Friday's BoJ decision, where any hawkish shift in tone would likely matter more for the yen than today's modest pullback in USD/JPY.
currencies.watchToday: Nothing further is scheduled for JPY today. Japan's national CPI print lands Thursday, setting the stage for Friday's Bank of Japan decision (rate currently 1.00%), where the central bank is expected to hold but may lean hawkish.

currencies.headline: Franc gains as broad dollar weakness outweighs fading haven demand.
currencies.commentary:
The franc has strengthened against the dollar this afternoon, even though the underlying reason for today's move, the US-Iran strike pause, would normally be expected to reduce demand for safe havens like the franc itself. In practice, the dollar's own broad-based retreat has outweighed any softening in haven flows, leaving CHF a net beneficiary of the session.

That dynamic is a useful reminder that the franc doesn't always move in a simple risk-on, risk-off pattern: today it's tracking the dollar's weakness more than any change in risk appetite. With no Swiss data due this week, CHF is likely to keep taking its cues from the broader dollar story, particularly Wednesday's Fed decision, rather than domestic developments.
currencies.watchToday: No CHF-specific events are scheduled this week. CHF trading is likely to keep following the broader dollar and safe-haven flows around Wednesday's Fed decision rather than anything scheduled domestically.

currencies.headline: Loonie lags the broader dollar retreat as oil's sharp slide bites.
currencies.commentary:
The Canadian dollar has held onto earlier losses this afternoon even as the broader dollar softens, with USD/CAD staying elevated. The reason is straightforward: Brent crude has tumbled roughly 9% today after the US and Iran paused hostilities, and with Canada a major energy exporter, that drop has outweighed the dollar weakness that's lifting most other majors today.

It's a clear illustration of how CAD can swim against the tide when oil moves sharply: a softer dollar would normally help the loonie, but a 9% single-day drop in crude is a bigger force in the other direction. With the Bank of Canada's next decision some weeks away, oil prices and any further developments in the Middle East ceasefire are likely to matter more for CAD than the broader dollar story for now.
currencies.watchToday: No Canadian data remains scheduled for today. With the Bank of Canada's next decision some weeks away, the loonie is likely to stay driven mainly by oil prices and Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Kiwi holds firm as hawkish RBNZ bets meet a softer dollar.
currencies.commentary:
The New Zealand dollar has stayed firm this afternoon, up slightly on the day. It opened the week on the front foot thanks to lingering hawkish expectations after this month's RBNZ hike, and the broader dollar retreat following the US-Iran strike pause has given it a further, if modest, tailwind.

Improved risk appetite tied to easing Middle East tensions has also helped, since the kiwi tends to trade like a barometer for broader global sentiment. The bigger swing factor for NZD this week remains oil: New Zealand's reliance on imported fuel means today's sharp drop in crude is a genuine net positive for the inflation outlook, even as it complicates the picture for other, oil-exporting currencies like CAD.
currencies.watchToday: No New Zealand data is due for the remainder of today. With the next RBNZ meeting not until September, the kiwi is likely to stay reactive to broader dollar moves and Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Aussie firms as softer dollar and calmer oil market both help.
currencies.commentary:
AUD/USD has pushed higher this afternoon, supported by the same broad dollar weakness lifting most majors today. The sharp fall in oil prices following the US-Iran strike pause has also eased a source of imported inflation pressure, which is a modest net positive for a currency that's historically been sensitive to global risk sentiment.

China remains the other key swing factor for the Australian dollar given how much of the country's exports go there, and today's session hasn't changed that underlying picture. With Australian inflation and labour market data due before the 11 August RBA meeting, AUD/USD looks likely to stay within its recent broad range for now rather than break out decisively in either direction.
currencies.watchToday: No Australian data remains scheduled for today. RBA Governor Michele Bullock speaks tomorrow morning (04:05 UK time), which markets will watch closely for any signal ahead of the Bank's mid-August meeting.

currencies.headline: Yuan strengthens to a six-week high as dollar demand eases.
currencies.commentary:
The offshore yuan has firmed to its strongest level since mid-June this afternoon, as the broader retreat in the dollar following the US-Iran strike pause has reduced demand for the greenback across the board. The move continues a period of relative yuan stability that's been reinforced by the PBoC's recent steps to deepen Hong Kong's role as an offshore trading hub.

As with most emerging and Asian currencies today, the yuan's gain reflects a broad dollar story rather than anything China-specific: the PBoC has given no fresh signal on rates and continues to manage the currency mainly through its daily fixing rather than large moves. That measured approach is part of why CNY remains one of the least volatile major currencies clients trade day to day, even on a session with this much dollar movement elsewhere.
currencies.watchToday: No CNY-specific events are scheduled this week. The yuan's daily fixing and any fresh PBoC commentary remain the main things to watch, alongside the broader dollar direction into Wednesday's Fed decision.

currencies.headline: Rand rallies sharply as oil's slide reverses this morning's weakness.
currencies.commentary:
The rand has staged a strong recovery this afternoon, well off the weaker levels seen earlier today, as Brent crude's roughly 9% drop following the US-Iran strike pause has taken significant pressure off an oil-importing economy like South Africa's. With a broad dollar retreat adding to the move, the rand's rebound looks larger than that of most other emerging market currencies today.

The scale of the move is a reminder of how directly South Africa's currency is exposed to swings in oil prices, given the country imports the bulk of its fuel needs. With no SARB meeting scheduled this week, the rand is likely to stay sensitive to further developments in the Middle East ceasefire and the broader dollar story around Wednesday's Fed decision, rather than domestic news, for the rest of the week.
currencies.watchToday: No SARB meeting is scheduled this week, so the rand is likely to stay driven by external factors, particularly any further developments in the Middle East and Wednesday's Fed decision, rather than domestic news.
